authority.decision_rule: Any conflict with the accepted capability specifications, constitution, accepted ADRs, the T007 ownership register, the T008 requirement register, the T009 architecture model, the accepted unit designs, or an accepted predecessor candidate is resolved in favour of the accepted source; material gaps are recorded, not guessed. XDL1 (XDL Lite Phase 1) is accepted and merged; its requirement baseline XDL1-SR-001..019 and all inherited records remain untouched. ARGUS2 (Argus Lite Phase 2) is additive and bounded: it derives ARGUS2-SR-001..012 from the admitted thesis Phase 2 planning inputs and the accepted REF-002 allocation register, adds one bounded evidence allocation per selected parent in the admitted order (original parent IDs/sections/owners/dispositions preserved, no new system requirement IDs, no parent closed), and specifies only an offline Python evidence package that persists a bounded versioned causal event stream plus an atomic run manifest, imports an owned X-COM observation projection, and reconstructs evidence read-only. It changes no legacy, compat, blueprint, accepted C++ X-COM, assurance/oracle, accepted XDL schema or API, or historical record. Authority for orchestration, actuation, provider delivery, metrics computation, dashboards and oracles stays outside Argus. The accepted platform baseline for this feature is platform main c1fd213cd00259b74f8308d8ca58157ea985aaa0. Measured runtime outcomes, X-COM interoperability, compatibility/parity, live readiness, and delivery acceptance are external gates and are not claimed by this project pointer. Direct Codex successor: the author explicitly requested abort and direct repair on 2026-10-02; this supersedes the Fabro-only route for P2-FINISH. Current assembled baseline is 947ac1e58e2b97f2cd6d6cdb33bc1b3c3bdc7f6b. Original c1fd213 baseline remains planning history. Evidence and acceptance are defined by codex-direct-repair.md and its external bundle; historical stage records do not verify this successor.

reliability.basis: Bounded, single-writer, offline Python evidence persistence over an explicitly admitted run envelope: Argus verifies the accepted semantic plan digest through the accepted xverse_xdl.experiment_plan public API, appends validated events to a versioned JSONL stream, publishes an atomic run manifest with artifact identities/sizes/hashes and explicit evidence obligations, imports a documented versioned projection of owned C++ X-COM ObservationRecord values with preserved payload visibility and loss semantics, and reconstructs evidence read-only with deterministic selection, caller-configured finite bounds, explicit clock domains and stable structured diagnostics. No control, actuation, metric computation, network, oracle, live-tap or production activity; each stage's evidence is bound to the exact candidate revision and reviewed separately.

boundaries: Bounded Phase 2 Argus Lite scope: the ARGUS2 requirement/architecture/unit/verification/validation records, docs/engineering/argus-lite/** work products, the offline evidence package src/xverse/argus/**, owned neutral fixtures and tests under tests/thesis_lite/argus/**, additive xverse namespace/package wheel configuration in pyproject.toml, additive engineering/trace/links.json links, engineering/stage-results/argus2-*.json, and reports/argus-lite/**.

No change to legacy, compat, blueprint, accepted C++ X-COM source or contracts, assurance/oracle logic, accepted XDL v1alpha1 schemas, the accepted public experiment-plan/loader/normalizer/validator/catalog APIs, the existing xdl CLI, existing tests, or any historical accepted requirement/design/unit/measure/validation/stage record or ADR.

No runtime, live or production execution: no component start or lifecycle action, no fault activation, no live tap attach/pull, no provider-delivery change, no metrics computation, no dashboard, no oracle access, no network or extra dependency/runtime service, no production workload and no legacy execution; Phase 3 (Maestro Lite) and later capabilities are not started.
scope.intended_use: Let an experiment caller supply an accepted resolved experiment plan and run envelope, a unique run identity, explicit producer/clock identities and finite limits/obligations, then persist bounded events together with an imported owned X-COM observation projection and publish an atomic run manifest; and later let a reader reconstruct that evidence read-only through JSON/JSONL export with verified hashes and declared metric-input links. Successful finalization proves only that the caller-declared capture obligations were verified; it never proves scientific validity, safety, compatibility, parity or live readiness.
success_criteria: Exactly 12 bounded software requirements (ARGUS2-SR-001..012), one per selected REF-002 parent in the admitted order, with the original parent IDs/sections/owners/dispositions preserved and no new system requirement IDs.

A created run verifies the accepted semantic plan digest, keeps semantic plan identity separate from source-byte provenance, appends only validated events to a versioned JSONL stream, and publishes an atomic manifest whose artifact identities, sizes and hashes verify on read.

Evidence completeness is reported honestly: an unmet obligation, truncated last record, missing or mutated artifact, unsafe path, known observation loss, unavailable interval closure or clock/causal uncertainty is reported as incomplete, damaged or unresolved and never upgraded to complete.

The real accepted XDL compiler output and a real owned C++ X-COM observation-record producer fixture (compiled with accepted headers/implementation, no public API change) are imported and exercised, and the built wheel installs offline and imports xverse.argus plus the existing xverse_xdl API outside the source tree with an empty PYTHONPATH.
A separate read-only internal review and terminal user acceptance precede the exact isolated merge and verification into platform main.

title: ARGUS2 Argus Lite Phase 2 - bounded run evidence persistence and read-only reconstruction
verification_profile_note: Trusted policy requires explicit unit, static-analysis, whole-system integration, and validation measures bound to the exact candidate revision; ARGUS2 neither defines nor replaces that external policy and is exercised through its scoped ARGUS2-UNIT, ARGUS2-STATIC, ARGUS2-INTEGRATION, and ARGUS2-VALIDATION measure records. Source-only or mock checks cannot satisfy the whole-system integration gate, which is assembled and run in the pinned target checkout by the trusted host policy over the installed wheel.
